answer.generated: Mutual exclusion ensures that at most one process can hold a resource at any time, which prevents circular wait by guaranteeing that no two processes simultaneously request exclusive access to the same resource. When mutual exclusion is violated, processes may acquire multiple resources while waiting for others, leading to deadlock where each holds a resource and waits for another. This condition must be enforced strictly to avoid situations where resources are held indefinitely.
